Subject: Request: strict region-only routing for PHI workloads

Hi Priya,

Quick note from compliance: MediCore is preparing to send a pilot set of PHI-protected transcripts to Redwood for inference. Their security team requires that all inference for these records be served from the us-west-2 region only — no automatic routing to other regions or failover variants is permitted under their certificate. Thanks,
Daniel Hart

Thanks Priya — quick reality check from Policy/Product:

1) Feasibility: Yes, we can create a customer-specific routing rule that pins requests to a single region and a single model endpoint. That is a configuration-layer change (routing policy DB + matching rule). It will prevent the standard multi-region fallback policy from triggering for that customer ID.

2) Risk/implications: The main tradeoffs are availability and operational burden. If the single region experiences an outage or capacity pressure, the request will queue or fail rather than automatically routing elsewhere. That increases MTTR obligations and may require a contract exception for availability. Also, per-token costs may rise if we need reserved capacity.

3) Observability & audit: We must add explicit telemetry: route decision logs, request headers showing policy ID, and an audit flag on the customer's tokens so Legal & Security can verify no cross-region routes occurred. We'll also need a short runbook for manual failover and a confirmation flow with the customer before any manual action.

4) Suggested compromise: For a short-term pilot, propose an enforced-primary-region mode where we pin to us-west-2 but allow a documented manual failover with an approval flow (email + Ops ticket). This preserves compliance posture while giving us an escape hatch for incident recovery. If the customer insists on absolutely no manual fallback, that must be escalated to Sales + Legal for commercial acceptance of higher risk and a modified SLA.

ETA: policy config + logging changes — ~4 business days; if we need reserved capacity and capacity testing, add 5–7 business days.

I'll draft the minimal policy change and required telemetry after we confirm approach.

— Karthik Iyer
Head of Product (Routing)
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-23T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: strict region-only routing for PHI workloads

Technical notes from Infra:

- Implementation steps:
  1) Add a routing policy flag 'region_enforce' on the customer's policy record that bypasses the multi-region router for matching requests.
  2) Emit a \"region_enforce=true\" field in request logs and a signed proof-of-route entry for each request (for audit).
  3) If customer needs guaranteed capacity, create a short-lived reserved capacity pool in us-west-2 and test load.

- Performance: locking to a single region has negligible per-request latency impact when healthy. The real impact is on throughput headroom if we do not autoscale across regions. If we do reserved capacity, cost is predictable but higher.

- Edge cases: model upgrades and pinned-model variants. If we pin a model binary in us-west-2, any hotfix will require coordinated rollout. We should add a 'model_maintenance_window' field to the policy so the customer accepts manual maintenance notifications.

- ETA: conservative turnaround for a pilot (policy + telemetry + test): 6 business days. With parallel work on reserved capacity we can be ready in ~9 business days.

Attachments: redwood_exception_form.csv (template for capturing customer sign-off)

Happy to kick off a short engineering spike if Sales wants a hard date.

— Dev Patel
Staff Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
